summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: corporate wellness arrives as visual clutter over an ordinary workday. Middle image: Astra and Kreeb identify the contradiction and the one potentially useful provision. Closing image: Zib points to the physical station behind the program.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Wellness Baseline Week banners cover the operations level while ordinary station work continues underneath them.
PANEL 2 — Astra reads the required-participation / optional-disclosure language with coffee still in hand.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb finds the quiet-room provision in the packet and marks it as the first potentially useful element.
PANEL 4 — Zib taps the wall hidden behind one of the banners, bringing the real maintenance problem into the opening page.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: That's one useful thing before coffee. I'll take it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: There's another useful thing behind that banner.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Please tell me it isn't load-bearing.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Multipurpose Room. Opening image: the room conversion creates the physical conflict immediately. Middle image: a ten-minute repair collides with a day-long program schedule. Closing image: Astra knowingly delays the work for one block.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The multipurpose room is fully dressed for the program; the largest screen and chair arc visibly block the ventilation service chase.
PANEL 2 — Zib shows Astra the ten-minute damper ticket at the blocked wall.
PANEL 3 — Pixa displays the room schedule, with the first open access window pushed to late day.
PANEL 4 — Astra weighs the morning block against the maintenance delay while Zib states the physical consequence.
PANEL 5 — Astra allows one session block to proceed and Zib records the delay rather than arguing further.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: That is what the word means.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: First open access window is eighteen-thirty.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: It is ten in the morning.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can it wait through the first block?

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: One block. Then you get the wall.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Quiet Room. Opening image: the alternative room is deliberately plain. Middle image: Glorp solves the tracking problem without invading the room. Closing image: Kreeb accepts the practical compromise.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Kreeb prepares the adjacent quiet room with plain chairs, water and no program branding.
PANEL 2 — Glorp studies the utilization requirement at the doorway and relocates the tracking point into the hall instead of the room.
PANEL 3 — Pixa confirms anonymous entry counting with identity and dwell time disabled while Kreeb checks the settings himself.
PANEL 4 — Glorp leaves the counter outside and Kreeb opens the door, the compromise already working without a committee scene.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: If I count entries only, the room can stay private.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the tracker mistakes an ordinary delay for a wellness event. Middle image: Jax tests the absurdity with Pixa. Closing image: Astra passes through without stopping the workday.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax waits beside a cargo lift with a parts cart as his tracker announces a mindful pause.
PANEL 2 — Jax argues with Pixa about whether ordinary waiting has accidentally become wellness.
PANEL 3 — Astra passes with the multipurpose-room schedule and warns Jax not to become a case study before lunch.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I am waiting for a lift.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Can I bill wellness for the delay?

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Then this is already less relaxing.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Please don't become a case study before lunch.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Multipurpose Room. Opening image: Noola experiences the delayed maintenance as a physical condition rather than an abstract metric. Middle image: Zib identifies the blocked access as the reason. Closing image: Astra acknowledges Noola's agency before the session starts.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Noola arrives in the multipurpose room in her water-dome rig while people are still settling into the required session.
PANEL 2 — She checks the heavier condensation and looks toward the room controls before speaking.
PANEL 3 — Zib points to the blocked service chase while Kreeb reminds Noola that the quiet room is available.
PANEL 4 — Astra catches the practical exchange and explicitly leaves Noola free to leave whenever she chooses.

dialogueInline.speaker: NOOLA
dialogueInline.text: Is it always this warm in here?

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: It's warmer because I can't get to that wall.

dialogueInline.speaker: NOOLA
dialogueInline.text: I know where the door is.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: And you can use it whenever you want.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Multipurpose Room, continuing directly from Noola's arrival. Opening image: the scene widens from comfort to instrumentation. Middle image: the room is already a compromised experiment. Closing image: Mira keeps the physical curiosity while rejecting the institutional claim.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira arrives carrying more environmental instrumentation than the wellness packet requires.
PANEL 2 — She places temperature and airflow sensors at different heights while Astra corrects her own terminology.
PANEL 3 — Pixa offers the staff-condition fields; Mira dismisses them while calibrating the physical sensors.
PANEL 4 — Astra asks whether anything useful can still come from a room with a known maintenance problem.
PANEL 5 — Mira admires the instrumentation and makes clear that useful room data is not the same thing as useful wellness evidence.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: The room is already wrong. I don't need a feelings column for that.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Can we get anything useful out of this?

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Multipurpose Room, continuing the same morning session. Opening image: the official program finally starts. Middle image: the unresolved physical problem continues underneath it. Closing image: the door remains an explicit option.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The baseline block begins; synthetic calm audio fills the already-warm room.
PANEL 2 — Zib watches the temperature and reminds Astra that the damper still needs ten minutes.
PANEL 3 — Noola adjusts her dome cooling while Kreeb keeps the exit path visibly available.
PANEL 4 — Astra confirms that anyone may leave, refusing to turn required participation into physical confinement.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: If you want out, go. We are not holding people hostage for wellness.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Multipurpose Room, continuing the session. Opening image: Noola acts on her own limit. Middle image: the exit becomes contagious without becoming theatrical. Closing image: the physical condition and participation failure become inseparable for Astra.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Noola decides the room is too warm and stands immediately, without waiting for a program prompt.
PANEL 2 — Pixa clears the doorway and Kreeb opens it; Noola exits and two other workers follow.
PANEL 3 — Mira records the three-degree rise while Pixa records exits without assigning motives.
PANEL 4 — Astra looks from the open door to the blocked service chase and finally sees one operational event instead of two separate program metrics.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: All right. I understand this problem.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Multipurpose Room, continuing directly after the exits. Opening image: the remaining head count becomes morally and scientifically useless. Middle image: Astra stops defending baseline completeness. Closing image: the room is handed back to maintenance.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax lingers by the door and offers to stay only if Astra needs the count; Astra refuses to use him that way.
PANEL 2 — Mira shows that the baseline is already compromised by the known room condition, and Astra owns the original delay decision.
PANEL 3 — Kreeb starts clearing the room before the final order, trusting where the conversation is going.
PANEL 4 — Astra ends the baseline block and gives Zib the wall.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I can stay if you need the head count.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: I don't need you sitting there for the spreadsheet.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: It went bad when I made Zib wait.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: End the block. Zib, take the wall.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Multipurpose Room, continuing the same scene as the program space becomes a work site. Opening image: the timer ends. Middle image: everyone finds a practical job clearing the room. Closing image: Zib finally gets the wall he asked for hours earlier.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Pixa ends the session timer as the room begins changing function.
PANEL 2 — Jax unplugs the speaker and jokes with Pixa while people start clearing equipment.
PANEL 3 — Pixa takes the speaker cart and rolls it out of the service path, volunteering physical help.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb stacks chairs and the HONOR THE PRESENT MOMENT placard winds up against a tool case.
PANEL 5 — Zib reaches the service panel at last and opens it.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Put it on my permanent record.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: There is no permanent wellness record.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: Best thing we've done all morning.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Multipurpose Room, continuing the repair. Opening image: the fault is small and legible. Middle image: the three-hour delay collapses into a ten-minute mechanical fix. Closing image: the room visibly recovers before any wellness interpretation can catch up.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Zib exposes the binding hinge immediately once the service chase is open.
PANEL 2 — Astra reacts to how ordinary the fault is while Mira reminds her how long Zib has been waiting.
PANEL 3 — Zib frees the hinge and cycles the damper.
PANEL 4 — Airflow returns; paper edges and Noola's earlier condensation cues visually reverse while Pixa and Mira report the physical recovery.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Can we just call it airflow?

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Multipurpose Room later that day. Opening image: the repaired room is useful again without a program. Middle image: Jax and Noola return for ordinary reasons while Kreeb restores only the practical amenities. Closing image: Zib closes the actual repair as normal room use resumes.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Later, the repaired multipurpose room is cooler and the wellness equipment is pushed aside; no official session is running.
PANEL 2 — Jax returns for his abandoned coffee and tests the room with exaggerated caution.
PANEL 3 — Noola enters, checks her dome temperature once and chooses a chair without comment from anyone else.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb returns the water pitcher without restarting the program or asking for reflection.
PANEL 5 — Zib closes the service log at the doorway while coworkers occupy the room for ordinary reasons.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: It was a speaker and a hot room.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: Keep me out of the report.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the administrative problem arrives only after the physical one is solved. Middle image: Glorp independently discovers the useful distinction in the form. Closing image: Kreeb's prepared argument turns into ordinary coworker teasing.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Back in operations, Glorp opens the interrupted-session record and notices that participation and reflection are separate fields.
PANEL 2 — He rereads the distinction rather than immediately calling Kreeb over.
PANEL 3 — Pixa confirms the fields can be completed independently while Glorp closes a test no-entry record.
PANEL 4 — Kreeb arrives ready to object and discovers that Glorp has already protected the no-entry state.
PANEL 5 — Astra approves the local rule while Glorp enjoys, briefly, having solved the problem first.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Participation and reflection may be completed separately.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: So they can participate and leave reflection blank.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: Save it for the next form.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: Jax's messy day enters the same system. Middle image: Noola's very different participation record joins it. Closing image: Glorp accepts both without forcing them into the same story.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax turns in a tracker that records ordinary waiting, an early exit, speaker moving and no disclosure.
PANEL 2 — Noola turns in her shorter record with the room-temperature exit and no disclosure.
PANEL 3 — Glorp checks both records and finds that they are equally complete despite describing different days.
PANEL 4 — Jax tries to make the symmetry sentimental and Glorp refuses.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: I waited for a lift, sat in a hot room, left, moved a speaker, and told nobody anything.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Quiet Room. Opening image: Astra nearly reproduces the wellness-program behavior in the refuge. Middle image: Noola redirects her with dry literalism. Closing image: the only question that remains is practical and welcome.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — In the quiet room, Astra opens the door with the report in hand and starts to ask Noola a broader question.
PANEL 2 — Noola's literal answer stops the check-in from becoming another program conversation; Astra narrows the question to room temperature.
PANEL 3 — Noola answers the physical question, Kreeb approves, and Astra accepts that restraint as progress.

dialogueInline.speaker: KREEB
dialogueInline.text: See? That one I can answer.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Multipurpose Room. Opening image: Mira turns the day into a physical timeline. Middle image: the one clean causal chain is mechanical. Closing image: the room recovery is legible while wellness attribution remains deliberately absent.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Mira lays out the room timeline with before, during, repair and after states.
PANEL 2 — The temperature rise is visible beside the beginning of the session.
PANEL 3 — Session exits are shown in the same period without assigning a common motive.
PANEL 4 — Zib's damper repair sits at the center of the sequence as the clear intervention that actually occurred.
PANEL 5 — Temperature and airflow recover afterward while the wellness claim remains outside the physical conclusion.

dialogueInline.speaker: ZIB
dialogueInline.text: You could put my name next to that.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: I don't know. That's not in this data.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the final report starts from the actual day. Middle image: Mira, Glorp and Kreeb react to its unusual clarity. Closing image: Astra sends the readable version.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra drafts the report beside the repaired-room trace rather than beside a wellness dashboard.
PANEL 2 — Mira enjoys the simple hot-room / repaired-damper / recovered-room sequence for what it is.
PANEL 3 — Glorp and Kreeb react to how readable the report has become.
PANEL 4 — Astra sends it before anyone can complicate the wording.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: Because the room got hot and then we fixed it.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: Before anybody changes it, I'm sending it.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing directly from the submitted report. Opening image: the reply arrives before the scene clears. Middle image: corporate treats low disclosure as a limitation. Closing image: the same required/optional contradiction returns under a new program name.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The corporate reply arrives with THANK YOU FOR THE LEARNINGS and Astra immediately distrusts the tone.
PANEL 2 — LOW DISCLOSURE CONTEXT LIMITS INTERPRETABILITY appears as the first substantive response.
PANEL 3 — The supplemental voluntary-disclosure initiative appears beneath it.
PANEL 4 — Astra rejects the framing while Pixa explains that participation is required even though disclosure remains optional.

dialogueInline.speaker: PIXA
dialogueInline.text: Participation is required. Disclosure remains optional.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: I liked you better when you were moving the speaker.

summary: Primary composition: 4-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub, continuing the same response scene. Opening image: Astra reacts to the institutional lesson. Middle image: Kreeb and Mira reveal different personal wins. Closing image: the crew's takeaways remain plural rather than being forced into one meaning.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Astra keeps the new program open long enough to complain that almost no feelings produced yet another feelings program.
PANEL 2 — Kreeb points to the preserved NO ENTRY rule as the boundary worth keeping.
PANEL 3 — Mira is already looking back at the airflow curve from the repaired room instead of the new program.
PANEL 4 — Astra realizes they each took a different useful thing from the failed week.

dialogueInline.speaker: ASTRA
dialogueInline.text: We gave them a hot room and no disclosures, and they built another program.

dialogueInline.speaker: MIRA
dialogueInline.text: And I kept the airflow data.

summary: Primary composition: 5-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the program closes through an ordinary desk handoff. Middle image: Glorp accepts a complete record with no disclosure and no interpretive addition. Closing image: Jax leaves him to keep adapting.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — Jax drops his completed tracker on Glorp's desk and summarizes the absurdly ordinary day it records.
PANEL 2 — Glorp checks the tracker against the local no-entry rule.
PANEL 3 — Glorp confirms that every part of the record is accurate without adding interpretation.
PANEL 4 — Jax notices Glorp's adjustment to a form that permits absence and needles him about it.
PANEL 5 — Jax heads back to work while Glorp leaves the completed no-entry record visible on his desk.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: For the record: participated, disclosed nothing, moved one speaker.

dialogueInline.speaker: GLORP
dialogueInline.text: I am adapting to a form that permits absence.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Multipurpose Room. Opening image: the program branding disappears. Middle image: one locally useful rule survives. Closing image: the room returns to normal with the boundary left behind.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — The corporate wellness banners come down from the multipurpose room, exposing the ordinary wall and repaired access again.
PANEL 2 — One small local sign remains: NO ENTRY IS VALID.
PANEL 3 — Astra refuses to make the guidance temporary while Glorp and Kreeb return to their familiar bickering.

summary: Primary composition: 3-panel page in Main Bullpen / Admin Hub. Opening image: the next program arrives immediately. Middle image: Jax and Noola treat the new language through what they just learned. Closing image: Astra's one-day reassurance becomes the tag.

panelPlan.text: PANEL 1 — A printer produces the fresh BRING YOUR FEELINGS TO WORK DAY placard over the required-participation / optional-disclosure language.
PANEL 2 — Jax and Noola read it together; Noola reminds him that bringing nothing is now a proven option.
PANEL 3 — Astra checks the date and confirms they only have to survive one day, which does not reassure Jax.

dialogueInline.speaker: SIGN
dialogueInline.text: BRING YOUR FEELINGS TO WORK DAY.

dialogueInline.speaker: NOOLA
dialogueInline.text: You just did it all week.

dialogueInline.speaker: JAX
dialogueInline.text: That's what you said about the week.
